why: The defect is real. In places.md, Foreign room says the principal's own device-seat pins and stamped versions "stay trusted and keep restoring, to runs that had a seat in it". Pin says a pin restores "to runs that have had a seat in its room during the run, or whose agent's earlier runs had one (REC-02)". The index.md relation carries "every room its agent's earlier runs had a seat in (PIN-10, REC-02)" and defers to Foreign room only for which pins restore ("once the room is foreign only those Foreign room names"). Agent says later runs inherit rooms for restore but "never a seat". So a later run of the agent, which holds no seat in the foreign room, gets these pins under Pin and the hub relation and loses them under Foreign room. DM-AC's closing texts never reached places.md, so the round-1 closing text is incomplete. PIN-10, REC-02 and the PIN-10 scenario already settle the rule: the foreign-room limit narrows only which pins qualify, not which runs get them. The scenario's later run has no seat in the foreign room "L5" and still gets that room's pins.

why: The defect is real. The default pin budget is 1,000 model tokens. For a long-lived agent with a stable harness agent id, every inherited room's intent, and any inherited pin with a lower priority number, comes before the current room's constraints. Those constraints then show only by id and count. I3 still holds, since omitted pins are named by id and count, so this is a usefulness gap, not an invariant break. why:
The defect is real. It applies once PRV-10 ships, when other principals' seats and trust grants exist.

How a room act drops pins:
- Foreign room counts "a room every seat of its principal has left or lost to a kick or a bar" as foreign. There, only "its principal's own device-seat pins and the versions it stamped stay trusted and keep restoring".
- The index.md relation says "a leave, kick or bar keeps them, but once the room is foreign only those Foreign room names".
- Room act says "A leave, kick or bar never drops a room's qualifying pins from a run's restore block, within the foreign-room limit of Relations".
- An agent leaves by its own tool call: `room_leave` "records the seat's leave (LANE-23)".

A principal's only member seat in another principal's room is often a run seat; a trust grant that covers every room is recorded in the personal room, so the principal's device seat never joins. Then two things each make the room foreign and remove every trust-granted pin from every restore block of that principal's agents, including the leaving run's own:
- an agent steered by untrusted content calls `room_leave`;
- another principal, such as an appointed moderator, kicks or bars that last seat.

Why this contradicts the rest of the model:
- OWN-11 and Acts and roles: "Any principal act that removes a pin from a restore block ... is widening whatever verb carries it".
- "A pin, edit or unpin room act never changes any restore block".
- Room acts "on their own ... never widen what reaches an agent".
- LANE-26: "a device-seat pin it removes MUST raise a Needs you item for its author's principal and keep restoring to every agent it restored to until that principal unpins it".
- SEC-32: an appointed moderator "MUST NOT change another seat's pin or make a list removal".

Earlier rounds settled the parts but not this combination:
- Round 20 Q1: a leave, kick or bar drops no pin.
- Round 21 Q1: trust-granted pins stop in a foreign room.
- Round 30 Q3: a room every seat left or lost is foreign.
- The PIN-10 scenario's "L5" case asserts that a kick drops the trust-granted pin.

No requirement or ADR decides whether a room act that the principal did not take may cause that drop. The foreign-room carve-out was added as a consistency fix (round 22), not as a security decision.

options.label: No leave, kick or bar drops a pin; what qualified is kept as it stood
options.effect: A leave, kick or bar never drops a pin from any restore block. In a room it makes foreign, the pins that qualified for the principal's agents keep restoring to the runs PIN-10 names, trust-granted pins included. They keep the state they had in causal order before that act, which is deterministic (I10). They stay until the principal's own act changes them: revoking the grant (OWN-11 already excepts that cut), unstamping, quarantining or rejoining. Versions written after the act gain nothing from a trust grant, so round 21 Q1's limit still holds for anything new, and recall still marks the room untrusted (RCL-10). This closes both the injected `room_leave` path and the other-principal kick or bar path, consistent with round 20 Q1, LANE-26 and SEC-32. The PIN-10 scenario's "L5" outcome changes: the trust-granted pin restores by its version from before the kick.

options.label: Close only the agent's path
options.effect: A run seat's `room_leave` that would leave its principal with no member seat in a room it does not own is refused, audited and counted. It goes ahead only if its principal asks for it at a principal surface, a widening principal act like asking for a join (LANE-23). Kicks and bars keep today's effect, and each raises a Needs you item naming the trust-granted pins that stop restoring, which the principal may keep by stamping them. The PIN-10 scenario and rounds 21 and 30 stay as they are. Another principal's room act can still remove pins from this principal's agents. Agents can no longer leave such rooms on their own, and the principal-asked leave is a new act the model must take in.

options.label: Keep the rule and make it visible
options.effect: No behavior change. A leave, kick or bar that makes a room foreign is audited and raises a Needs you item naming the trust-granted pins that stop, which a stamp can keep. An injected `room_leave` still removes those constraints until the principal acts, which still contradicts OWN-11's rule that removing a pin from a restore block needs a widening act of the agent's own principal.

recommendation:
Option 1. It is the safe choice, because no act the agent's own principal did not take can remove constraints from its agents' restore blocks. It also gives one rule, consistent with round 20 Q1, LANE-26's list removal, SEC-32 and OWN-11. Round 21 Q1 and round 30 Q3 still apply to everything written after the act, so no new text from another principal becomes trusted in a foreign room. No invariant wording changes: I2 and I8 already trust what a standing trust grant covers.

The edits cover the model (Foreign room, the hub relation, Room act, Trust grant, Pin, Intent), the SRS (PIN-10, OWN-29, PRV-02, RCL-10, VIEW-07) and the scenarios (PIN-10's "L5" case and the foreign-room line of PRV-02's scenario). Trusted sources already defers to Foreign room. Run `mdsmith fix .` afterwards to realign the changed SRS table rows.

Size: acts-and-roles.md is at 2,990 of 3,000 tokens. The Room-act edit keeps the same word count, and mdsmith still reads 2,990 after all edits. With every REG-1, REG-8 and REG-3 edit applied in any order, every model file passes mdsmith; only the SRS tables need `mdsmith fix`. All new lines are 80 columns or fewer.

why: Real. The model's Trust grant entry (docs/domain-model/trust-and-flow.md) says only that a grant naming a service account "whose certificate or managed-policy listing marks it as relaying text others wrote, or whose listing is unmarked, is refused". OWN-29 says the same, and only as a rule on recording: "It MUST NOT name a service account its certificate or managed-policy listing marks as relaying text others wrote ... a listing without the mark counting as relaying". Two cases slip through. (1) The grant is recorded while the key set holds no certificate for the key, so "A principal key never certified counts as a person's" (principals-and-agents.md), and a relay-marked certificate or an unmarked managed-policy listing arrives later. (2) The grant replicates to another of the grantor's nodes whose key set already holds such a certificate or listing. In both cases nothing stops coverage. Yet the Trust level entry says trust is "derived ... from ... the node's key set ... and that principal's stamps and trust grants as its writer logs carry them (I10)", and I10 requires the result to be "independent of the order in which logs arrived". So coverage that depends on what arrived first breaks I10, and a relaying account's third-party text would then reach the grantor's agents as trusted (I2, T28). DM-L's closing text puts listings into the key set ("each managed-policy listing and each removal of one is recorded as a structural event that enters the node's key set"). That makes a derived, order-free rule possible but does not state one. The fix says "holds", and the key set already includes revocations, so a certificate revoked later still counts. That keeps revoking a certificate, a cut act, from ever widening what a grant covers.
settled_by: ADR-2610061700 decision 2 (I2, what a trust grant carries), approved by the stakeholder: "It never covers run seats or relaying service accounts, so no agent's text becomes trusted through it." With I10: "a deterministic function of the set of writer logs a node holds and the node's own key set, independent of the order in which logs arrived." The SRS (OWN-29, PRV-10) states only the refusal at record time and the marking, so the model and the SRS need to carry the standing rule.
recommendation: Carry ADR-2610061700's "never covers relaying service accounts" as a derived, standing condition in the Trust grant entry, in OWN-29 and in the `parinn trust-grant record` row. Keep the refusal at record time. Add one OWN-29 scenario step so the rule is executable; it stays @pending. OWN-29's traces (I2, I6, I8) are left alone and I10 is cited only in the model, so no tag or appendix B change is needed. The OWN-29 and 09a table rows grow, so run `mdsmith fix .` afterwards to re-pad those tables. I checked this in a scratch copy: after the fix, `mdsmith check .` and `go test ./internal/... ./cmd/...` pass, the ledger gate included. trust-and-flow.md grows by about 35 words (now about 2120 words, 193 lines) and stays under 3000 tokens and 250 lines. These edits do not overlap REG-6's edit to the same entry, and the two can be applied in either order.

why: Real. The facilitator's device seat is an appointed moderator (Facilitator entry: "making that device seat an appointed moderator (SEC-32)"). An appointed moderator has "moderator capabilities only within SEC-32's limits" (LANE-16), and a moderator has "a contributor's capabilities", which include "pin, edit and unpin its own pins, its pin capability" (acts-and-roles.md Role). SEC-32 forbids only changing another seat's pin ("MUST NOT change another seat's pin or make a list removal"), so the facilitator may pin. OWN-29 covers "the posts and pins that principal wrote from device seats a device key of that principal certified", and its pins "MUST restore to them as the grantor's own pins would" (PIN-10). The own-words rule is stated for posts only. In SEC-32: "Its posts MUST be in its own words only ... never quote or embed it, so it relays no third party's text". In the model: "It posts only in its own words ... so it relays no third party's text (SEC-32)". The grant warning in the Trust grant entry says only "which its posts never quote". A facilitator reads untrusted room text by design (T27), so a swayed one can pin a marked range word for word. Under a grant that pin then restores verbatim as trusted in the grantor's restore blocks after every compaction (I3), the strongest channel I2 allows. That defeats the stated purpose of DM-V's closing text ("so it relays no third party's text") and is T28's trust laundering through a pin. Room summaries are already excluded (LANE-33: "no trust grant MAY cover it"), but pins are not. The DM-V cited texts are kept intact: the new text is added beside them, not reworded into them.
settled_by: none. No SRS row or ADR limits the facilitator's pin text. SEC-32's own-words rule names posts only ("Its posts MUST be in its own words only, shown as its own statements, that point by range link to the marked range each names and never quote or embed it, so it relays no third party's text"), and its purpose clause is the direction this edit completes.

why: The defect is real. DM-T's closing text in places.md says that on a node whose node identity changed "the events recorded before the change are another node's: they count as received ... and are trusted only as PRV-02 trusts received events (I8)". REC-24 says the same: "Every event recorded before the change MUST then count on the node as another node's, received and not recorded there". A quarantine is an `operator` event in the home's old device-seat writer, and it applies only "on the node that records it" (record.md Quarantine; SEC-12: "MUST take effect immediately for all recall, landmark and injection operations on the node that records it"). I5 adds: "A quarantine reaches another node only as a quarantine request that node's principal applies." So once the change makes the home's own quarantines another node's, the quarantine set (I10) stops deriving them. Quarantined content returns to recall. Once PRV-10 ships, a quarantined device-seat pin also returns to restore blocks, because its seat certificate chains to the principal key. The principal took no act for either. No rule says the home's quarantines survive the change. The SRS already decides the same lapse the other way for a backup restore: ADM-06 must "reinstate the segments, payloads and derived artifacts the copy contains" (the quarantine set is one) and "reapply every purge, revocation, quarantine ... recorded after the backup was taken or refuse". So completing DM-T in that direction is a tightening, not a new choice. Keeping the quarantines that were in force at the change keeps the principal's own home as it was. No quarantine reaches the node by exchange (PEER-11), and nothing widens: a release there stays a widening principal act (SEC-12). I5's wording therefore stands, and no ADR is needed. A neighbouring gap is outside this theme: before PRV-10, rule-level tightenings made before the change also lapse, because OWN-02 counts only "this node's own device seat". why: The defect is real. The Run entry in principals-and-agents.md says "a harness resume that starts a new harness session, or a harness clear, starts a new run", and that a run "carries its recall taint (SEC-13)". Recall taint (trust-and-flow.md) is "A run's mark after it recalls untrusted content, or inherited from the delegating run (OWN-24)". SEC-13 sets it only "when untrusted content has been returned to that run". A resume that starts a new harness session (§2: SessionStart with `source` = `resume` carries "a new one when it starts a new harness session") carries the resumed conversation into the new run. That includes the enveloped untrusted content the earlier run recalled. Yet nothing taints the new run, so OWN-10's "A recall-tainted run (SEC-13) MUST have the action classes SEC-13 configures as sensitive tightened one level" stops applying exactly while that content is still in the agent's context. OWN-24 already sets the direction: the taint follows the context, and a delegate "MUST inherit the delegating run's recall taint (SEC-13)". The other cases need no change. A harness clear carries no context, only a trusted restore block. A retry from a worktree checkpoint carries "no content of the earlier run except what the new run recalls" (OWN-28). A resume that keeps its harness session, including one that loses its run-seat key (DM-D, OQ-43), stays the same run and keeps its taint. The hook gives only the new session id, so ParleyInn may not be able to tell which run a resume resumes. In that case CLAUDE.md's rule "Where usefulness and safety conflict, pick safety" settles it: the run carries taint from its first event. This is a tightening that follows from SEC-13, OWN-10 and OWN-24, not a stakeholder choice. It does not touch DM-E's agent-identity decision. Size: trust-and-flow.md grows to 193 lines (about 1489 heuristic tokens). A trial copy passes `mdsmith check .` and the Go gate tests.

recommendation: State in the model's Recall taint entry, and in SEC-13 (keeping its SHOULD), that a run a harness resume starts carries the recall taint of the run it resumes, and carries taint from its first event when ParleyInn cannot tell which run that is. Add both cases as Then steps to SEC-13's pending scenario. After the string replace, run `mdsmith fix` on docs/srs/06-security.md so the table row is re-padded. The Run entry needs no change, since it already defers to recall taint (SEC-13).

why: Real. The model says a witness check runs "with network, the OS user's home directory (`HOME`) and the principal's home (its platform key-store entries included) denied" and "Unless the platform can deny all three, ParleyInn refuses". OWN-18, boundary register row 25 ("network, `HOME` and the principal's home (its key-store entries included) denied") and the `parinn witness-check start` row in 09a say the same. So the check's code, which comes from an untrusted commit and runs outside any agent sandbox, keeps every other write the OS user has. ADM-13 lets the launcher make fresh checkouts and new worktrees that add no ref, so a checkout can share the repository's git directory. The code can then write `hooks/` or `config` there, or edit a sibling worktree outside `HOME`, and that code later runs unconfined when the person commits or builds. That is a way out of the sandbox for a sandboxed agent. ADM-13 and SEC-18 do not close it: they bind only ParleyInn's own writes ("ParleyInn MUST NOT write to any git repository or worktree ... except ... the launcher's fresh checkouts"), not the program the launcher starts, which row 25 lists as its own process. The same escape exists through local endpoints. The check runs as the same OS user, so 'network denied' (a network namespace) still lets it reach Unix-socket endpoints: the container runtime's socket, the ssh agent, or the launcher's own same-UID endpoint (SEC-29, T21). Through those it can start code unconfined. The edit therefore denies local endpoints too. That is the same class of escape, so the rule is completed in the direction DM-AB already took (deny it, or refuse the check), not reopened. Mechanical checks: mdsmith check passes on a scratch copy with these edits and `mdsmith fix` (table re-padding). git-and-forge.md becomes 94 lines and about 1,350 tokens. DM-AB's ledger quotes from the model and OWN-18 ("Unless the platform can deny all three ...", "Unless the platform can deny it all three ...") no longer match and must be re-pointed to the new wording; its 06b quote still matches.
settled_by: none. ADM-13 ("ParleyInn MUST NOT write to any git repository or worktree (objects, refs, notes, git configuration, git hooks or files), except ... the launcher's fresh checkouts and new worktrees outside the run's worktree") and SEC-18 ("ParleyInn MUST NOT write inside the run's repository except where ADM-13 allows") bind only ParleyInn's own writes, not the witness-check command the launcher starts (06b row 25).
recommendation: Complete DM-AB's closing text in its own direction. Besides network, `HOME` and the principal's home, also deny local endpoints and every write outside the fresh checkout, the repository's git directory and its other worktrees included. ParleyInn still refuses before confirmation, naming what the platform cannot deny. Apply the same rule in the model (Witness check), OWN-18, 06b row 25, the 09a `parinn witness-check start` row and the OWN-18 scenario, which gains a step proving that a write to the git directory or to another worktree changes nothing. Run `mdsmith fix` to re-pad the 06b and 09a tables, and re-point DM-AB's two ledger quotes to the new text. The "local endpoints" part goes beyond the finding's quote. If the stakeholder wants this theme scoped to writes only, drop it and raise it as its own finding.

why: Real. The model says a subagent has "no seat in its parent's rooms but those it joins as Join says, which ParleyInn may suggest (LANE-23)". LANE-23 requires an ask or acceptance per run ("MUST NOT join either without that acceptance") and says nothing about one act covering a run's subagents. LANE-01 routes a run's events "to its run seat in the room it works in, one it joined or created ... while that seat is a member with work ...; else to its personal-room seat, never refused". So until its principal accepts a join for that one subagent run, usually after the short-lived subagent has ended, the subagent's events, edits and checks on the room's branch land in the private personal room. They stay outside the room's history and results, and the room's pins never reach its restore block. Commits it makes still carry the room trailer (LANE-28), so other principals see commits whose work they cannot read. An event goes to exactly one writer for good, so a later acceptance cannot move these events. Whether one act may cover a run's subagents is a real choice. Earlier rulings frame it: the stakeholder held that a subagent joins its parent's rooms only on acceptance, that later runs of an agent inherit no seat, and that joining stays explicit. Any fix must keep the join an explicit act of the principal. Mechanical checks: 05b-lane-requirements.md is at about 7,997 of its 8,000-token mdsmith budget. The SRS edit is kept word-neutral by dropping LANE-23's restatement "tied to its parent's run by its parent link, as MUST any other joining run", which REC-02 already states ("each subagent as a separate run, tied to its parent's run by a parent link"). With that trim, mdsmith check passes on a scratch copy at 7,999 tokens, so any other theme that adds to 05b must trim too. principals-and-agents.md becomes 111 lines and about 1,630 tokens. The Owner entry and LANE-16 need no change. A covering act of the owner is the owner's act joining its own (subagent) run, so DM-AD's "its act joining its own run assigns that seat contributor (LANE-16)" already gives each covered seat contributor. The scenario checks this, and DM-Y's and DM-AD's ledger quotes stay intact.
settled_by: none. LANE-23 says only "ParleyInn MAY suggest joining a run to a room that names its worktree's branch, and a subagent to its parent's rooms, and MUST NOT join either without that acceptance" and "A subagent that joins MUST get its own seat id". It is silent on whether one ask or acceptance may cover a run's subagents. The stakeholder ruled (round 1) that "a subagent joins its parent's rooms only on acceptance (LANE-23)".

options.label: A. Opt-in cover on the run's join (recommended)
options.effect: An ask for, or acceptance of, a run's join is a widening principal act. It may say that it also covers the run's subagents. Each subagent then joins by that act, with its own seat id and seat key, under the room's admission, but only while the parent run's seat is a member, so a kick or leave of the parent stops further subagent joins. Where the act is the owner's for its own run, LANE-16 gives each covered seat contributor; another principal's covered seats get the role an invite names, or viewer. An act that does not say so covers no subagent, and ParleyInn may still suggest each subagent's join. Joining stays explicit, and only the agent's own principal widens what reaches the subagent (I2).

options.label: B. Per-subagent acceptance only (status quo, made explicit)
options.effect: No new act. The model and LANE-23 state that a subagent's events stay in its personal room until its principal accepts that subagent's own join. This is the safest option and adds no surface, but a short-lived subagent's work on the room's branch stays outside the room's history and results, and the room's pins never reach its restore block. The finding stays open as a known usefulness gap.

options.label: C. Subagents join their parent's rooms automatically
options.effect: Every subagent of a run with a seat in a room joins that room at its start, with no principal act naming the cover. All of the room's work is recorded in the room, but this reverses the stakeholder's ruling that a subagent joins only on acceptance and LANE-23's "joining any room MUST stay explicit". It widens what reaches each subagent (room pins, directed posts) without any act of its principal that names the cover.

recommendation: Option A. It finishes DM-Y in the direction already decided: a subagent still joins only on its principal's explicit acceptance, which may now be given in advance on the run's join and is shown and recorded as a widening principal act. It is off unless that act says so, and holds only while the parent run's seat is a member, so a kick or leave cannot be bypassed through subagents. Edits: the model's Subagent entry; LANE-23, with a word-neutral trim of a clause REC-02 already states, because 05b is at its token budget; `--subagents` on `parinn run join` and `parinn join-request accept` in 09a; and the LANE-23 scenario. Run `mdsmith fix` afterwards to re-pad the 09a table.
